paragraph: Single-family is the Tenafly market, with 68 sales over six months at a median of $1,700,000, and the typical sale is a four or five bedroom colonial with three full baths. Half the sales closed above list and the median time to contract was 18 days, but the sale-to-list ratio sits right at asking, so read this as competitive rather than frenzied. Well-priced homes move quickly and you should expect competition on the good ones. Sales ran from $555,000 to $6,650,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. Volume built exactly the way it should into summer, 19 closings in June and 18 in July against six to ten in late winter and spring. June's $2,400,000 median came from a run of high-end closings; July's pullback to $1,662,500 on nearly the same volume is a mix shift toward more ordinary houses, not a price drop. Condos and townhouses are thin here, 8 sales at a median of $698,500, mostly two-bedroom, two-bath units, and eight sales is too small to read as a trend. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance lifestyle of a condo.
